description: Complex Romano-British farmstead established in the early 2nd CE. A rectangular timber building on the roadside, followed by a polygonal masonry building in the mid 2nd CE, these structures have been interpreted as a wayside shrine. Later the site experienced a decline but still showed occupation in the 4th CE.
bibliography: Martyn, Blick, Brindle, and et al. “Portway (Gloucestershire).” The Rural Settlement of Roman Britain: an online resource, 2015. https://doi.org/10.5284/1030449.
Rawes. “The Romano-British Site on the Portway, near Gloucester.” Trans Bristol and Gloucestershire Archaeological Society 102 (1984).
